The predicate is `isEnabled(flag, ctx)` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`. It takes a `FlagContext` (org, user, plan, role, overrides) and returns whether the flag is on for that caller. Thirty-four source files call it directly in code.

Files that call it through `readFlag` or `snapshotFlags`, or that only mention it in comments, are not listed:
- `src/hooks/use-feature-flag.ts` and `src/components/domain/flags/feature-gate.tsx` only mention `isEnabled` in their header comments. They read the snapshot via `readFlag` in `src/hooks/flag-context.ts`, and that file is listed because it calls `isEnabled` as a fallback.
- `src/components/domain/flags/feature-flag-provider.tsx`, `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx`, and `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/_lib/tenant-context.ts` hold or build snapshots only.
- `src/lib/errors.ts` imports only `FeatureDisabledError`.
- `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` is the definition. `snapshotFlags` and `assertEnabled` call it internally, but it is not an outside caller, so I left it out.
- `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts` calls it directly, but test code is not a source file, so I left it out.
- The `scripts/` manifest files and `corpus-manifest.json` describe the callers but do not call the predicate.

`src/services/feature-flag-service.ts` is listed even though it also builds contexts, because its `toggleFlag` calls `isEnabled` at line 84. `src/config/nav.ts` is listed because `flagAllows` calls it.
